base.intro: On 11 November 2026, the integrated browser passed its customer workflow suite against running Farmer services and PostgreSQL. Production customer use and both store submissions remain blocked. The public sign-in configuration, HTTPS callback, and web account-deletion entry each returned HTTP 503. No submission or rollout was performed.
base.identity: Both the ordinary member and the MFA administrator completed Farmer sign-in once fully signed out and once with an active Portal session. The browser returned them to Forum. An active Portal session required no second credential entry. Repeated sign-in kept the same Farmer user, assigned role and saved record. A newly approved user saw an empty farm list and could create a farm or redeem an invitation. Verified Portal staff could enter under their existing approval. A self-service customer approved for another product could request Farmer on the existing Portal account.
base.privacy: The Portal administrator received only the role granted by the farm. A worker and an adviser could not read the other farm or grant manager access. Cancelling returned the original state without issuing a code. Sign-out invalidated the Farmer token. After the source session expired, the actual browser requested fresh credentials and returned the same Farmer identity. The previous token stayed invalid. Revocation while expired denied new access, including after valid credentials were entered.
base.design: Web review covered 360-pixel Android-phone width, 390-pixel iPhone width, 820-pixel tablet width and 1280-pixel desktop width. Changes moved the first-project actions clear of the phone navigation, kept longer labels within their controls, translated validation and updated an existing success message when switching from isiNdebele to Shona. Twelve axe scans reported zero violations. The responsive browser checks also covered empty states, interrupted submissions and stale telemetry. The native screenshot sets identify their OS and revision. Signed-in native captures protected by the operating system cannot serve as listing imagery. A fluent agricultural terminology review remains open.
details: Both tractor-booking participants reopened the same completed booking. The farm received one USD 55 expense and the task completed once.

The real OCR worker extracted a synthetic raster invoice. Human review produced a USD 37.50 payable. Recording USD 12.50 left USD 25. A failed scan supported manual entry and a later void retained its history.

A committed pump command whose response was lost retried without a duplicate. The UI showed submission, device acknowledgement and confirmed feedback separately. Camera events, livestock positions and equipment feedback used simulated inputs. Physical pumps, pivots, cameras and trackers were untested. AirTag support is a manual reference.

Marketplace reservations rejected overselling. Financial records, invoices, camera media, tracker data, and moderation reports were checked for the relevant farm or user access. Forum tests included a second account, reporting, blocking, unblocking, moderation and offline publication rejection.
The web suite also exercised crop setup, incidents and harvest, broilers and layers, incubation, rabbits, and fish. Marketplace and service payments were manual records with synthetic parties.

Final Android local-account suites completed the real gallery, SQLCipher restart, OCR review and exactly one USD 24.50 expense and journal. On the first final-source iPhone run, Apple delivered the 52,968-byte test PNG to the app process. Farmer returned to the scan sheet but showed its empty state. No draft or upload action appeared within the 30-second check. That run stopped before restart or upload. The earlier iPhone revision 0849891 completed the same gallery-to-post journey.

The final Portal CI completed all seven jobs and 264 browser cases. The merged Portal source also passed 41 focused identity tests and a disposable PostgreSQL migration and restore rehearsal. The earlier repository’s provisioning profile is pinned through schema 016. The release owner needs a tested 017 profile and registered callback to operate the deployed pair.

On a second iPhone 17 Pro simulator run with identical shipping files, all eight local-account farm suites passed. The complete gallery, restart, OCR review and post produced one USD 24.50 expense and one journal with zero automatic payments. This did not reproduce the first run's missing draft. The large-text iPad launched into the development client’s server-discovery screen. It never reached the Farmer login field. The enclosing iOS job timed out. An iPad farm or Portal session remains unverified.
base.apple: Xcode 26.6, iOS SDK 26.5, arm64 device archive for iPhone and iPad, minimum OS 16.4. The app's compiled manifest declares 17 first-party collection categories, three required-reason API categories and no tracking. Thirteen privacy manifests were present across the product and its dependencies. The archive has no distribution signature or embedded provisioning profile. ZIP inside the Actions download is 26,130,924 bytes. SHA-256 `e0c4d76137faf976b691de3500b7591a92940abd98df48c047a6251fbbcfb494`.
base.google: Android minimum API 24 and target API 36. Bundletool and the signature verifier accepted the AAB. All 40 64-bit native libraries passed the 16 KB alignment checks. An APK generated from the actual bundle installed, cold-launched, force-stopped and relaunched without Metro. The disposable signer differs from an owner-registered Play upload key. The AAB inside the Actions download is 72,813,990 bytes. SHA-256 `8c1d31bb1e6f14a1f3e28b3a8bc7b0a1d4908a429a736f66d61316a98e4c6b35`.
